findings.description: The EBS volume attached to the portal server is created without an encrypted flag and without a KMS key, so the disk's data is stored unencrypted and readable by anyone who obtains the underlying volume or snapshot.

map_public_ip_on_launch is true on a subnet associated with a route table that has a 0.0.0.0/0 route to an internet gateway, so any instance launched here receives a public IP and is directly reachable from the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true on this subnet, which is also associated with the internet-routed route table portal_routes, exposing instances launched in it to the public internet by default.

The EC2 user_data script embeds a literal AWS access key ID and secret access key (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMAAA / wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMAAAKEY). user_data is readable from instance metadata and via the EC2 API by anyone with DescribeInstanceAttribute permission, so these long-lived credentials are effectively disclosed.
The ingress rule allows TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administration of the instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.

TCP/80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, publishing the web service to the public internet with no network boundary. Combined with the open SSH rule and the plaintext user_data credentials this instance is directly reachable by any host.

The S3 bucket used as the VPC flow log destination has no server-side encryption configuration, so flow log records (which capture source/destination IPs, ports and traffic metadata) are stored unencrypted at rest.

The bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and no bucket policy restricting access, and force_destroy = true allows the contents to be destroyed with the bucket. Without S3 Block Public Access the bucket relies on defaults alone to prevent public exposure of the flow log archive.
